land.text: 'the Gododdin seem to have come under the rule of Bernicia around this time' (638); Bernicia then became part of Northumbria

capitals.name: Din Eidyn (Edinburgh)
capitals.note: 'According to tradition, local kings of this period lived at both Traprain Law and Din Eidyn'; the infobox has no capital.

correction.text: 'the area known as the Hen Ogledd or Old North' including 'what are now the Lothian and Borders regions of eastern Scotland'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Gododdin (its Brythons rows cover the north). 'It is not known exactly how far the kingdom of the Gododdin extended'; bounded 'to the west by the Brittonic Kingdom of Strathclyde, and to the north by the Picts'. No area on the page; the Tweed and Northumberland are not described as Votadini land.

region.text: the Votadini's lands in Lothian and the Borders

ledger.note: The Gododdin, 'Descendants of the Votadini': infobox 'Established: circa 4th century'; Cunedda 'is supposed to have been a Manaw Gododdin warlord who migrated southwest during the 5th century'. 350 is a rounding of 'circa 4th century'.

region.text: Lothian and the Borders, after Din Eidyn fell

ledger.note: 638: Din Eidyn falls to the Angles. 'In 638, Eidyn, modern Edinburgh, was under siege and fell to the Angles'; 'the Gododdin seem to have come under the rule of Bernicia around this time'. The page gives no disestablishment date; the infobox period is c. 550 to c. 650. [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Counterpart was kingdom-of-bernicia, whose dossier ends in 634 (merged into Northumbria); in 638 the Angles who took Din Eidyn ('In 638, Eidyn ... was under siege and fell to the Angles', Gododdin page) are Northumbria's (Cliopatria row kingdom-of-northumbria, 612-935).

wars.name: Battle of Catraeth
wars.outcome: 'In around 600 the Gododdin raised a force of about 300 men to assault the Angle stronghold of Catraeth'; it 'ended disastrously for the Britons' and is memorialised in the poem Y Gododdin.

wars.name: Siege of Din Eidyn
wars.outcome: Edinburgh 'under siege and fell to the Angles'; Bernicia rules the area afterwards.

certainty.note: The page says the extent is not known exactly.

notes: Eu-11-a and eu-11-f asked for a gododdin dossier. Page budget: one page. The disestablishment is inferred from the fall of Din Eidyn; the page gives none. Mynyddog Mwynfawr is not on the page. Bernicia (kingdom-of-bernicia) is another part's dossier.
